analysis.title: JPM International Market Intelligence - Morning Briefing (November 11, 2026)
key_insights: Global risk-on with Tech leading as AI optimism returns, with TSMC and CRWV helping the bounce. US equities lagged global peers after hot US CPI and hawkish Fed comments.

A sharp UST selloff followed the CPI print and Fed comments. The US 2Y had its biggest move since Apr-25 and the selloff spilled into global rates. Markets price the possibility of a 50bps Fed hike in December.

US inflation concerns are returning while energy prices fall. Brent broke below $90 after Trump pulled back strike threats, and US-led RU/UA peace talks resume today. The commodities desk sees Brent fair value at $80-$85.

Oil and LNG flows through the Strait of Hormuz (SOH) are normalizing but strikes continue. TTF gas prices should stay elevated given colder weather (counter to the El Niño pattern) and a renewables shortfall accelerating storage withdrawals.

The improving geopolitical narrative has been a clear positive for Europe and international equities. India stands out, with the rally extending on foreign net buying and net foreign equity outflows having bottomed out.
Broadening supports the EM trade via lower oil prices, declining bond yields, and a weaker or stable dollar. Thematic focus should remain on non-AI as well.
After the October neocloud meltdown, CRWV eased funding anxieties by disclosing it will rely more on customer prepayments than additional borrowing.
JPM Credit Strategists say asset managers have led buying of hyperscaler bonds so far. Insurers remain underweight, with scope to add as 'price creates capacity'.
JPM Research turned more cautious on AI-linked US Electricals names but expects a sharp bounce given the speed of the selloff. Sustaining it requires improving customer ROIs on AI spend.
Post midterms, GPU rental prices are the key thing to watch as a measure of compute scarcity.

Japan flows: Japanese investors net bought ¥0.5tn of foreign bonds in August, driven by pension funds (¥0.8tn). BoP data through September shows no evidence of EUR-denominated bond selling, and MoF October data does not signal a GPIF allocation shift.

Japanese FX margin traders keep building short JPY exposure in JPY crosses while trimming short JPY against USD. Retail investors net bought ¥1tn of foreign equities for a fourth straight month in October. JPM sees the JGB uptick as deposit-funded and expects retail demand for foreign equities to stay intact.

China trade: exports eased from September's high but remained strong, with mixed tech and softer autos and consumer goods. Imports rose on energy and tech supply chain needs. The surplus narrowed but the full-year total is on track to exceed last year's.

JPM is tactically bullish on global equities. It prefers long US and Asia (Japan, South Korea, Taiwan) versus Europe. The US is overheating, Europe is recovering from stagflation, and Asia has pockets of both.

Broadening can return more clearly in the US than in Europe. European earnings fundamentals are good and positioning gives a buy signal, but EGB spread stability is needed for conviction in EU broadening.

Longs: tech and supercycle themes (inference, semi cap, less-levered hyperscalers, AI-vulnerables including application software), cyclicals with secular tailwinds (EU and JA banks, EU industrials, JA machinery, GE Infra, EU miners), EU Pharma, UKX, and selective consumer.
Shorts: AI-vulnerables ex-software, short-cycle data center capex names, EU insurance, challenged industries (autos, chemicals, Asian consumer electronics, MedTech) and MDAX.

Positioning: Multi-Strat de-grossing was the largest 20-day event since Covid. After 20-day gross flows first fell below the 5th percentile (Oct. 27), alpha was higher over the next 20 days in 9 of 10 cases.

HF net leverage fell about 4% over the week to near 12-month lows. Eq L/S net leverage is at a three-year low and global momentum exposure is near three-year lows. Semis were the most net-sold US theme and EMEA short covering hit a 3z extreme.

risk_factors: US inflation re-accelerating, with markets pricing a possible 50bps Fed hike in December.
Strikes continue despite normalizing oil and LNG flows through the Strait of Hormuz.
TTF prices could stay elevated on cold weather and a renewables shortfall.
A lack of improving customer ROIs on AI spend could undermine the bounce in AI-linked names.
EGB spread instability could hold back EU broadening.
Hedge fund alpha is uncertain and past midterm years saw December recoveries coincide with market sell-offs.
Upcoming market catalysts could have a big impact on HF and market direction.
vol_and_positioning: Multi-Strat 20-day de-grossing was the largest since Covid. After 20-day gross flows first fell below the 5th percentile (Oct. 27), alpha was higher over the following 20 days in 9 of 10 cases.

In the past five years, HFs rebounded over the following 5 and 10 days in all eight comparable events where 5- and 20-day net returns fell below -2z. Late Feb 2020 and late Oct 2018 were followed by further losses.

HF net leverage fell about 4% over the past week to near 12-month lows. Eq L/S net leverage is at a three-year low and All Strategy net leverage is near the 40th percentile on a three-/five-year basis.
Global momentum exposure is near three-year lows. Semis were the most net-sold US theme, software flows were neutral, and AI-cyclical exposure fell quickly.
EMEA and China/HK saw HF net buying while North America and Japan saw net selling. European short covering reached a 3z extreme, last seen in late 2022.
Option hedges: keep MCX < UKX until clarity emerges, and short FR vs EU Domestics.
geopolitical: Trump pulled back strike threats, and US-led RU/UA peace talks resume today.
Oil and LNG flows through the Strait of Hormuz are normalizing, but strikes continue.
US Congress returns after the Democrats' midterm win.
G7 foreign ministers meet in Paris.
EU finance ministers meet on the bloc's 2027 budget.
France politics are cited as a basis for the short FR vs EU Domestics hedge.
